subject: Request: signed vulnerability artifact manifest + CVE remediation attestation
messages:
From: Jarret Mulcahy <jarret@finedge.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: security@finedge.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: signed vuln artifact manifest + CVE remediation attestation

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review and our upcoming audit window, InfoSec needs a short artifact packet that contains: a signed vulnerability artifact manifest (hashes of the scan outputs for the reporting period), a statement of scan cadence/SLA, and a signed CVE remediation attestation covering any open critical/high items in the last 90 days.

Specifically:
- Manifest should list scan files (filename + sha256) for scans from 2026-09-01 through 2026-10-07.
- Scan cadence description (how often full infra scans run vs. targeted scans) and the SLA for remediation by severity.
- Attestation (PDF, signed) listing CVE IDs we remediated in the last 90d with fix dates and responsible owner.

Can you confirm what you can provide by EOD Wednesday (Oct 7)? Our auditor wants to bundle the items into the SIG submission. If any items require an exec sign-off, flag that and we'll coordinate.

Appreciate it,
Jarret
Jarret Mulcahy
Director, Information Security
FinEdge Payments

Attachment: none
From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: Jarret Mulcahy <jarret@finedge.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: signed vuln artifact manifest + CVE remediation attestation

Hi Jarret —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front: yes, we can produce the artifact manifest and the signed attestation PDF by EOD Wed (Oct 7). Below is what we'll include and one request about scope.

What we'll attach:
- redwood_vuln_manifest_20261007.pdf — index of scans + sha256 hashes for the period 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-07 (includes full infra weekly scans + ad-hoc triage scans).
- scan-hash-index-20261001-20261007.txt — plaintext index of individual scan result filenames and hashes for reproducibility.
- cve-attestation-signed-20261007.pdf — signed attestation covering remediation windows and fix dates for critical/high CVEs closed in the last 90 days.

Scan cadence / SLA summary (short):
- Full infrastructure vulnerability scan: weekly (every Monday 02:00 UTC).
- Targeted container/image scans: on-build (CI) + daily scheduled image registry sweep.
- Host-level authenticated scans for managed fleet: bi-weekly.

Remediation SLOs we commit to in the attestation:
- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or exploitable remote RCE): mitigate or workaround within 72 hours; full patch within 14 days when patch available.
- High (CVSS 7.0-8.9): mitigate or triage within 7 days; patch within 30 days.
- Medium/Low: prioritized per risk owner and tracked in Jira.

One question on scope: do you need proof of patch deployment (e.g., AMI rebuild IDs or container image digests) for each CVE, or is the attestation listing fix dates + links to the build artifacts sufficient? If you need build/digest evidence bundled, we can include a short digest list but it'll increase the packet size.

I'll prepare the signed PDFs and the hash index. Markus, could you review the CVE list (I will attach a CSV of the items we intend to attest to) and confirm the remediation dates? Soojin, can you sign off on the SLA language?

Thanks —
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Sr. Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com

Reviewed the draft CSV you dropped in the shared drive (thanks). I confirm the remediation dates for the rows I own. A couple of notes for Jarret:

- CVE-2026-2147 (container runtime escape) — mitigated by configuration lockdown on 2026-08-12; full runtime upgrade rolled 2026-09-10 (image digest: sha256:aa11bb22...). We will include the image digest lines in the manifest for verifiability.
- CVE-2026-3019 (third-party library) — backported patch applied to our service image 2026-09-27; build artifact link included.
- There are two low-severity findings in the registry flagged as accepted risk; we'll list them with rationale.

I'll validate the sha256s in the scan-hash-index and append a short note mapping each CVE to the build/digest evidence.

Markus

Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: signed vuln artifact manifest + CVE remediation attestation

Jarret —

Attached are the materials for your SIG/CAIQ pack. Summary below and quick notes on chain-of-custody.

Attachments (zipped for upload):
- redwood_vuln_manifest_20261007.pdf — index + SHA256 for all scan outputs for 2026-09-01 -> 2026-10-07. Includes a short table mapping CVE -> remediation owner -> fix date -> artifact/digest link.
- scan-hash-index-20261001-20261007.txt — plaintext list of scan result filenames and their sha256 values (we timestamped and notarized the index).
- cve-attestation-signed-20261007.pdf — signed by Soojin (Head of Security Ops) with formal SLA language and the remediation attestation for closed critical/high items.

Key points:
- Scan cadence: weekly full scans + CI on-build image scans + daily registry sweep (see doc, section 2).
- SLA: Critical 72h mitigation / 14d patch; High 7d / 30d — attested and signed.
- Evidence: where available we included image/container digests and AMI build IDs. Where a patch was not available (temporary mitigations), we included the compensating control description.

Chain-of-custody: files were exported from our internal scan archive, checksummed, and uploaded to a restricted Drive folder. The manifest includes a Notary timestamp (RFC3161-style) and the scan hash index. The signed attestation contains an approver block and a DocuSign envelope ID: DS-ENVELOPE-20261007-9Y2.

If you need granular deployment logs for any single CVE (e.g., kubectl rollout details or host patch job IDs), let me know which CVE and we'll extract the logs.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min screen share tomorrow if the auditor wants to walk the packet.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
